items.headline: Tonight/tomorrow: RBA Gov Bullock speaks 4:50pm CT; NZ inflation expectations 8:00pm CT (Q3 2.34%); CFTC Nov 10 COT due 3:30pm ET (delayed by Veterans Day); Tue: UK earnings 1:00am CT, US retail sales 7:30am CT (+0.2% m/m fcst), Nvidia earnings after the close, RBA minutes 6:30pm CT; Wed: UK CPI 1:00am CT (3.6% fcst), FOMC minutes 1:00pm CT.

Dollar holds a fresh 19-month high into the New York close — DXY ~103.59 (6th straight up); EUR/USD ~$1.1003, a 19-month low; GBP/USD ~$1.3189; USD/JPY ~159.55, capped below 160 by intervention watch; AUD/USD ~$0.6754; NZD/USD ~$0.5515. Dec Fed 25bp hike ~93-94%, 50bp tail ~6%.

Oil slides — Brent ~$92.29 (-2.7%), WTI ~$85.45 (-2.6%) as the IEA's Q4 surplus call (1.7 mb/d) lands with Hormuz flows nearly restored; Goldman sees Brent averaging $88 in 2027 and $78 by year-end as supply outstrips demand by ~2 mb/d.

Tech rout into the close — Nasdaq -1.3% midday, S&P -1.0%, Dow -0.6%; Nvidia -4% pre-market and Micron -6% as the AI trade unwinds into Nvidia earnings Tue after the close; Taiwan -6%, KOSPI -3.6% overnight. 10Y ~5.13%, 2Y ~4.88%.

Fed Chair Warsh gives opening remarks at the Fed's Productivity and Jobs Task Force Conference (San Francisco) — Fed staff modeling three AI scenarios (productivity gains, job losses, stock slump); no rate proposal, no December steer. Dec 25bp hike ~93-94% stands; FOMC minutes Wed 1:00pm CT.

BoC Dec hike odds trimmed to ~44% after October CPI (Morningstar/Dow Jones, from ~60% pre-print; Polymarket 44.5% hike / 55% hold) — CPI +3.1% y/y vs 3.2% consensus, core anchored near 2%; hold stays the base case, January more likely. USD/CAD ~1.4297 into the close.

Empire State Manufacturing MISSES — +7.8 in November vs +16.7 expected (Oct 25.5, a multiyear high); new orders nearly stall at 3.0 (from 23.2), shipments 8.8; hiring jumps to 18.1, its highest since June 2022; prices paid ease to 45.9. A mixed soft read; Dec Fed hike pricing unmoved.

Canada CPI +3.1% y/y in October (vs 3.2% consensus; Sep 3.1%), +0.2% m/m (vs 0.3%); ex food & energy +1.8% y/y (vs 1.9%); BoC core median 2.0%, trim 1.8%, common 2.5% — core anchored near 2%, so the Dec 9 BoC hike case does not strengthen; hold stays the base case, January more likely (ING). USD/CAD ~1.4291 pre-print, probing the 1.4299 Oct top.

Today: Canada CPI 7:30am CT (RBC 3.0% y/y, core 1.9%; Sep 3.1%/2.1%) — the last big Canadian print before the Dec 9 BoC; Fed Chair Warsh speaks 11:00am CT (first set-piece since the Oct 28 hold); RBA Gov Bullock speaks 4:50pm CT; NZ inflation expectations 8:00pm CT; CFTC Nov 10 COT due 3:30pm ET (delayed by Veterans Day).

Israel security cabinet: no credible outcome reported as of late Sunday — the single-obscure-source radar-te.com item (Nov 15, 23:34 UTC) remains uncorroborated by any major wire; Eisenkot warned Netanyahu against security moves during the transition.

Eurozone industrial production MISSES — +0.2% m/m in September vs +0.3% expected (Aug -0.5%); -1.5% y/y vs -0.2% expected. First rise in four months, but ING: 'no signs of a true rebound', only modest gains ahead.

Gold slides to a 13-month low — spot $3,840.52 (-1%), intraday ~$3,832, lowest since Oct 2025; silver -3% to $47.25, also a one-year low; driver: DXY at its highest since Apr 2025 with ~94% odds of a Dec 25bp Fed hike; extends last week's 4.6% slide. Goldman cut its end-2027 gold forecast to $4,650.

Oil drifts lower in Asia — Brent $95.69 (-0.2%), WTI $88.68 (+0.1%) after the IEA surplus call (Q4 supply 105 mb/d, 1.7 mb/d above demand) and with Hormuz flows nearly restored; gold faded to ~$3,870 after an early $3,892 bounce (+0.3%), still -4.6% on last week.

China Oct activity triple miss — industrial output +4.8% y/y vs +5.3% fcst, retail sales +0.4% vs +0.8%, fixed-asset investment -8.1% vs -7.0%; AUD/USD edged just 0.09% lower at the print, $0.6763 in Asia.

Dollar extends gains for a fifth straight session — DXY 103.47, highest since Apr 2025; EUR/USD $1.1016 touches a 19-month low; Dec Fed 25bp ~92-94% (FedWatch 93.9% / futures 91.1%), 50bp tail ~6-8% (from 11.8% post-PPI). Schmid (KC Fed, Sun): inflation 'worryingly above target and moving in the wrong direction'.
items.source: Reuters Asia FX wrap (Gregor Stuart Hunter, Nov 16)

items.headline: Japan Q3 GDP contracts 0.1% annualized vs +0.3% expected — first contraction in a year; q/q 0.0% vs +0.1% fcst; consumption -0.3%, capex +1.6% beat, net exports -0.6pp drag. USD/JPY flat ~159.6-159.7 — the miss has not moved the yen or the Dec BoJ hike case (~84% intact); Katayama intervention warning still the cap near 160.

Reuters poll: most economists expect the ECB to deliver a final deposit-rate hike in December, more than a third expect another in early 2027 as inflation runs at double the 2% target; Dec hike ~88-92% priced. EUR/USD ~$1.1025 in Asia.

Dec Fed hike now priced ~91-94% for 25bp (CME FedWatch 93.9% via Reuters; Kalshi 96% any hike — 87.5% 25bp / 8.5% 50bp); markets also price a second hike in Jan at ~67% and a third by Mar at ~63%. Warsh speaks 11:00am CT today; FOMC minutes Wed 1:00pm CT.

IRGC claims a supertanker sank after hitting a mine in the southern Strait of Hormuz; UKMTO reports a separate attack on an eastbound energy tanker, crew safe, damage unknown — no vessel names, no independent confirmation of the sinking claim; Brent held near $95 despite the claims.

Bahrain issues nationwide alerts as IRGC claims second drone strike on US radar at Riffa — Bahrain MFA condemns the attack, says air defences intercepted the drones; Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan and Egypt condemn it too; no US confirmation of any hit; oil futures reopen 5pm CT.
items.source: UK Fact Check live blog / Daily Inference, Nov 15
